To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Rorschachs of patients with body‐cancer reveal that the body‐image of patients with body exterior cancer is significantly more likely than that of patients with body interior cancer to be enclosed by an im­penetrable boundary.
body‐image scores on the Rorschach are higher among patients with body‐external cancer than among patients with body internal cancer.

the Rorsch‐ach body‐image scores of patients with body‐cancer are related to the anatomical site of cancer, the relationship being such that patients with body‐external cancers tend to have a stronger body‐image than patients with body‐internal cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of body image to cancer site.
an attempt to demonstrate the relationship between body image and site of cancer.
the relationship between personality and the site of cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the body‐image scores of the Rorschach are a function of personality orientation and that this personality orientation is related to the development of cancer in a given site of the body.
the body‐image scores of the patients with exterior cancer are higher than those of patients with interior cancer.
the Rorschachs of patients with body‐external cancer show a greater degree of body‐image rigidity than do the Rorschachs from patients with body‐internal cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
patients with body‐exposed cancers have a greater tendency to think of their bodies as enclosed by an impermeable boundary than do patients with body‐covered cancers.

the Rorschachs of the body‐extterior cancer group are characterized by a greater tendency to perceive the body as a closed, impenetrable, and isolated entity than are the Rorschachs from the body‐intererior cancer group.
the body‐image scores of the Rorschach are a useful measure of the patient's tendency to conceive his body as a bounded entity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can’t just assume that a person with cancer will have a certain body image, and that their body image will be affected by cancer. Instead
the site of cancer is related to personality factors.
body image and cancer are linked.
